This PR successfully takes care of setting the correct SELinux label on `kubelet` binary for the test job `pull-kubernetes-node-crio-e2e`. As per the [kubelet logs](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/95035/pull-kubernetes-node-crio-e2e/1309750270489530368/artifacts/tmp-node-e2e-2873712d-fedora-coreos-32-20200907-3-0-gcp-x86-64/kubelet.log) from the test `pull-kubernetes-node-crio-e2e` is still failing because the cgroup driver for kubelet is incorrectly set to `cgroupfs` while crio is using `systemd`. 

I have fixed that in this [test-infra PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/19342) with [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/19342/commits/44f070a23f03be8f038f364fe920df58ed1b487f) commit. 

Once this PR merges, and kubekins image is rebuilt I will update https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/19342 with another commit that will use the new kubekins image.

I will remove the hold after that.

review_comments:
I am unfamiliar with SELinux, and so checking my understanding.
These binaries need to be added because they're not part of the distribution itself, and they weren't created on the OS, but were extracted/pushed/pulled from somewhere else.
Is that correct?

We had to add those SELinux labels explicitly because otherwise SELinux will prevent the execution of those binaries. By default, when you copy those binaries in certain location on the filesystem will not have those required labels.
Function name is more than only the Kubelet. Maybe drop Kubelet to `setSELinuxLabels`?
Ah, down below a stricter regex to find that and pull it out ahead of time.
